info.album: We Are Family - The Essential Sister Sledge

podcast.body: Kim Sledge stated that the group had committed to playing in Brussels, even at a point when the Pittsburgh Pirates were down three to one to Baltimore. This commitment meant they did not return to the States immediately. The song's lyrics are uncomplicated, but its significance stems from its powerful message of unity combined with the success of the Pittsburgh Pirates and the team's embrace of this message. Tracy Thompson emphasized that "We Are Family" represented unity to young black people on a national scale, making them feel connected to shared achievements. "The song we are family represents unity."

podcast.body: This song, by four sisters from Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, became the official clubhouse song of the 1979 Pittsburgh Pirates. It was first played during a rain delay at Pittsburgh's Three Rivers Stadium in early June 1979. Pirates legend Willie Stargell embraced it, influencing the team to adopt "The Family" as their identity, which was printed on their dugout and became synonymous with their World Series-winning run. The team even replaced "Take Me Out to the Ball Game" with it during the seventh-inning stretch. Sister Sledge learned of its popularity with the Pirates while on tour in Hamburg, Germany, hearing 50,000 people yelling the words. "We are family by sister sledge played over the stadium PA. And as the song came to an end, pirates legend Willie Stargel called up the press box. He told the PR director to announce that this was now the official clubhouse song of the Pittsburgh pirates."
